parsed.explanation: The combined regime is accepting on both law and society fronts. Self-determination gender recognition, equality law covering trans people in goods/services, hate-crime aggravation for 'change of sex', and marriage/adoption equality are all documented and current. Critically, no traveler-facing restriction is documented: no facility bans, no birth-sex custody rule (placement is case-by-case and protective, with chosen-name courtesy), no criminalisation of expression, and no documented police targeting or trans-specific violence pattern. Gaps — no gender-expression ground, no conversion-practice measures, no nonbinary marker — are climate signals, not visitor exposures. Thin-data absence of incident records in a well-governed, rights-active state is a moderately positive signal. Uncertainty remains on border document practice and non-resident recognition, but open questions are light, not exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; no border friction or marker-mismatch incidents reported.
entry_documents.protection: Foreign documents presumed accepted; no documented refusal or secondary-screening pattern for trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Whether non-residents may use the declaration procedure is unestablished, but irrelevant to entry on a home passport.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented as any trans-specific detention or investigation pattern.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented protective custody practice: case-by-case placement, requests for ordinary sections generally granted, chosen address honoured, ministerial warning against isolation (2015 answer).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Planned prison designed with separation sections; placement remains national, case-by-case.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility exclusion rules documented; no birth-sex placement rule codified.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Placement by disclosed identity/need; anti-stigmatisation ministerial guidance.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Prison design allows separation but operates without a codified birth-sex rule.

care_services.exposure: Not documented; no denial-of-care incidents for visitors.
care_services.protection: Equality law covers health and goods/services; action plan commits to equal healthcare treatment.
care_services.interaction: Depathologisation absent from 2025 plan; resident-facing gap, light visitor weight.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Not documented; no police profiling, raids or state demonisation of trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime aggravation for 'change of sex' in force; equality body handles complaints; 2019 gap later remedied.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Civil society active and consulted; institutions responsive to rights-body intervention.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visitors travelling with minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Minors may change gender status with guardian consent — resident-facing climate signal of institutional acceptance.
minors_guardians.interaction: No visitor-specific restriction affecting travelling families is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific violence pattern; under-reporting historically noted (2019) before aggravation remedy.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime aggravation now codified; functioning justice system.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Equality body and community organisation provide recourse channels.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: border document practice, enforcement data on aggravation use, action-plan implementation — unanswered questions, not exposures.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National equality body, active LGBTIQ+ organisation, 2025 action plan.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns resolve mildly upward given documented functioning institutions; absence of records in a rights-active state is a moderate positive.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.95-A shows audited, actively enforced border equality machinery and published oversight. This dossier shows strong law but lacks documented operational enforcement evidence on travelers specifically, so it sits a step below.
0.75-C involves documented secondary screening and humiliation risk at borders. No such traveler friction is documented here, and custody practice is affirmatively protective — clearly above 0.75-C.

Comparable: strong formal protections, no criminalisation, functioning remedies, minor residual uncertainties (marker practice, implementation detail). Sits in the same band, slightly below on unverified operational data.
0.65-A documents an actual outing-detention incident with imperfect officer discipline. No comparable incident exists here; this jurisdiction is above.

parsed.synthesis: Every documented traveler-facing element points the same direction: no criminalisation, no facility or custody restrictions, protective case-by-case detention placement, hate-crime aggravation in force, equality machinery and civil society operating, and marriage/adoption equality available even to couples read as same-sex under birth status. No single incident, pattern or statute weighs against the visitor. Remaining gaps (no gender-expression ground, no conversion-practice measures, no nonbinary marker, unverified border practice) are climate signals or light open questions in a well-documented, rights-responsive state. The score sits at the top of the Low Risk band, held off ~0.90+ only by the absence of positive documented operational evidence about travelers specifically.
